title.title: Fourier restriction for curved surfaces in three dimensions
title.subtitle: Claim: Fourier extension from a positively curved surface in $\mathbb R^3$ is bounded into $L^p$ for every $p > 3$

plain: How concentrated can a wave launched from a curved surface stay, far away? The sharp answer in 3D

beats.text: Extend a function off a curved surface by Fourier transform: which $L^p$ holds it?
The human record was $p > 22/7$, after Guth's $13/4$
The claim: every $p > 3$, for the sphere and every positively curved surface

steps: Measure how wave packets can bunch up: an 'elliptic capacity'
Show that capacity spreads along lines instead of piling up
Add decoupling, and the Kakeya estimate for general surfaces
